a1
Judah gave his firstborn, Er, a wife named Tamar. Er displeased the Lord, and the Lord took his life.
a2
Judah told Onan: marry your brother's widow. Onan would not give her a child, and the Lord took his life too.
b1
Judah told Tamar: stay a widow in your father's house until my son Shelah is grown. But he feared Shelah would die too.
b2
Years passed. Shelah grew up, but Tamar was not given to him.
c1
She covered her face with a veil and sat by the road. Judah did not know her. He left his seal, cord, and staff, and she conceived.
c2
Three months later Judah heard Tamar was pregnant, and said: bring her out, and let her be burned.
d1
She sent him the seal, cord, and staff. Judah said: she is more in the right than I.
d2
Tamar gave birth to twins, Perez and Zerah.
h1
Judah was ready to punish Tamar, yet he had kept Shelah from her.
h2
Shown his seal, cord, and staff, he did not argue. He admitted it.
h3
It takes courage to say: I was wrong.
h4
Today, stop defending one wrong, and make it right if you can.
i
What wrong do you need to admit?
